setup: A child care center staff member opens the Nenios Child Care Management web application in a browser.
action: The staff member navigates through the application as a center user.
expected_observation: The application presents child care management functions designed for a web-based child care center system, accessible through the browser interface.

setup: The child care center is using the system with family, child, attendance, invoice, and immunization data stored in a shared central database.
action: An administrator updates a child or family record and a staff member later accesses related operational information.
expected_observation: The updated information is available from the shared system view without re-entering the same data in separate records, supporting centralized information sharing and reducing duplicate administrative work.

setup: An administrator is signed in with permissions to manage enrollment, classroom capacity, and waiting lists.
action: The administrator registers a new family and reviews enrollment options for their child.
expected_observation: The system allows the family to be registered and provides enrollment management tools, including classroom capacity checks and waiting list handling when no space is available.

setup: An authorized staff member is signed in with permissions to access child care operations and customer information.
action: The staff member records a child immunization update, processes an invoice, and generates information needed by parents or center operations.
expected_observation: The system accepts the immunization update, completes invoice processing, and produces the requested customer or operational information for authorized use.

setup: A staff user with enrollment privileges is on the family registration screen in the child care management system.
action: The user enters a new family profile and the associated child details, then submits the registration.
expected_observation: The system creates the family and child records, confirms successful registration, and makes the child available for subsequent enrollment processing.

setup: A child has been selected for enrollment and the center's classroom capacity for the requested age group is already full.
action: An administrator checks whether a space is available for the child.
expected_observation: The system shows that no space is available and offers the option to place the child on the waiting list; if a space is available, it confirms availability for enrollment.

setup: A registered child exists in the system and classroom assignment rules and room capacities have been configured.
action: An administrator assigns the child to a classroom.
expected_observation: The system records the classroom assignment for the child and displays the assigned classroom in the child's record.

setup: A child record exists with stored immunization details, attendance history, and family contact information.
action: An authorized staff member updates the child's immunization status and changes the child's attendance or family details.
expected_observation: The system saves the revised child record and shows the updated immunization, attendance, and family information as current in the child profile.

setup: A child care account has active charges or a billing period ready for invoicing.
action: An authorized user generates an invoice for a family.
expected_observation: The system creates and displays the invoice with the correct billed items, amounts, and family account reference.

setup: A child is enrolled and expected at the center for the day, and the attendance screen is available to an authorized staff member.
action: The staff member checks the child in when they arrive and checks the child out when they leave.
expected_observation: The system records the check-in and check-out times for the child and updates the attendance record accordingly.

setup: Attendance records have already been captured for one or more children over a selected date range.
action: An authorized user opens the attendance review view and selects the date range to review.
expected_observation: The system displays the attendance history for the selected period, including each child's presence and absence information.

setup: A family record with stored contact information exists in the central database and the user has permission to view contact details.
action: The user searches for the family by name or child name.
expected_observation: The system returns the family's contact information, such as phone numbers and addresses, in the search results or family profile.

setup: A staff user with a defined access level opens a child's daily care profile.
action: The user views the child information page for daily care purposes.
expected_observation: The system displays only the child details permitted by the user's access level, including classroom assignment, contacts, immunization status, allergy alerts, and pickup-authority information as allowed.

setup: An authorized user is signed in to the system and operational data is available for reporting.
action: The user requests an operational report such as attendance, enrollment, or billing activity.
expected_observation: The system generates the requested report and presents it to the authorized user for review or export.

setup: A child immunization record exists with status values configured for the center's reporting needs.
action: A staff member opens the immunization record display for a child.
expected_observation: The system shows the immunization status using the supported categories current, due soon, overdue, exempt, or missing, as applicable to the record.

setup: A child's immunization profile exists in the system with several vaccine entries, and staff and the child's family are subscribed to compliance notifications for that child.
action: The immunization record reaches a status where one vaccine is nearing expiration, one is overdue, one is incomplete, and another required record is missing.
expected_observation: The child's immunization record is flagged with the appropriate compliance statuses, and the system notifies staff and the family with clear alerts indicating which records are nearing expiration, overdue, incomplete, expired, or missing.

setup: A family member is signed in to the family portal and the child has an existing immunization record that needs replacement.
action: The family uploads a new immunization document as a replacement record for the child.
expected_observation: The replacement immunization record is accepted into the child's file, becomes visible for review, and the system confirms that the document was uploaded successfully.

setup: A child is currently marked as not compliant because at least one immunization record is incomplete, overdue, expired, missing, or otherwise unacceptable.
action: The family uploads an updated immunization record, and staff have not yet reviewed or confirmed compliance.
expected_observation: The child remains marked as not compliant until the record is verified and staff explicitly confirm compliance; the compliance status does not change automatically upon upload alone.

setup: A family account is active and the family member is authenticated in the self-service portal with access to the child's profile, billing, and documents area.
action: The family updates contact information, submits or updates an enrollment form, opens invoice and payment history pages, and uploads a document from the portal.
expected_observation: The updated contact information is saved, the enrollment form submission is recorded, invoices and payment history are displayed to the family, and the uploaded document appears in the child's document list.

setup: A family member is signed into the portal and submits a request for a schedule change, contact change, enrollment change, billing-related update, pickup-authority change, or custody-related change that requires staff review.
action: The family submits the change request online.
expected_observation: The request is created with a pending review status, is not applied to the child's active record yet, and remains inactive until staff review and approve it.

setup: A family member is signed into the portal and is editing only a basic profile field such as address, phone number, email, or password without changing care arrangements or safety-related information.
action: The family saves the profile edit.
expected_observation: The updated address, phone number, email, or password takes effect immediately, and the change is reflected in the account without waiting for staff review.

setup: A family member is signed into the portal and is uploading a document that does not affect care arrangements or safety-related information.
action: The family submits the document upload.
expected_observation: The document is accepted immediately, becomes available in the family's document list, and no staff approval step is required before the upload is recorded.

setup: A family account has an outstanding invoice and the payer is using the online portal on a supported device with a valid payment method.
action: The payer submits payment through the online payment screen.
expected_observation: The payment is processed through the system, the invoice balance is updated, and the payer receives a confirmation that the online payment was accepted or completed.

setup: A family account is ready to make a payment through the portal and the payment method options are available.
action: The payer selects a credit card or debit card payment method, or selects bank transfer only if the system offers it as a secure option.
expected_observation: Credit card and debit card payments are accepted as supported payment methods, and bank transfer is offered only when the system can support it securely.

setup: A family invoice is open and the signed-in portal session belongs either to the account holder or to an authorized guardian linked to the account.
action: The authenticated account holder or authorized guardian submits a payment for the invoice.
expected_observation: The system accepts the payment from the account holder or authorized guardian and records it against the family account.

setup: An invoice has an outstanding balance and the family is making a payment that is less than the full amount due.
action: The payer submits a partial payment against the invoice.
expected_observation: The partial payment is recorded, the paid amount is applied to the invoice, and the invoice remains open with the remaining balance still due.

setup: A family member is attempting an online payment while staff are monitoring payment activity on the account.
action: The payment attempt fails due to a declined card, invalid payment details, or another payment processing error.
expected_observation: The failed payment is logged immediately, and both staff and the payer can see the failed transaction status right away.

setup: A payment is being made by a trusted family member or other non-account-holder in a rare exception case, and staff have either verified the person against account notes, obtained confirmation from the account holder, or received manager approval in an emergency.
action: Staff record the payment on behalf of the verified non-account-holder.
expected_observation: The system accepts the payment under the verified exception process and records the staff-validated identity or approval basis with the transaction.

setup: The classroom roster is configured with a defined maximum capacity and children are enrolled in that classroom.
action: The system calculates the number of currently enrolled children for the classroom.
expected_observation: The classroom record stores the maximum capacity and automatically tracks the enrolled child count against that limit.

setup: A classroom has a stored maximum capacity and a current enrollment count in the system.
action: A staff member views the classroom dashboard or roster page.
expected_observation: The screen displays the current enrolled count versus the classroom limit and clearly indicates whether the classroom is full or available.

setup: A classroom has reached its licensed capacity and is marked as full in the enrollment screen. A child from the waiting list is selected for enrollment.
action: A staff member attempts to add the waiting-list child to the full classroom without elevated permissions or removing another child first.
expected_observation: The system flags the classroom as full, prevents the enrollment from being completed, and displays a message that only a manager or administrator may override the limit or move a child off the waiting list.

setup: The waiting list contains multiple children with different requested start dates, priorities, and site preferences.
action: A staff member opens the waiting list review screen and filters or sorts the entries to review pending placements.
expected_observation: The system displays the waiting list entries with their relevant details and allows the staff member to review, update, and manage the list without affecting enrolled children.

setup: The center has defined room types and age or developmental stage rules for infant, toddler, preschool, and mixed-age classrooms. A child profile includes date of birth and developmental stage.
action: A staff member assigns the child to a classroom or changes the child's room assignment.
expected_observation: The system allows assignment only to a classroom or room type that matches the child's age or developmental stage, and it blocks or warns on assignments that do not meet the configured placement rules.

setup: A staff member is signed in to the dashboard or search screen with access to child and family records.
action: The staff member searches for a child or family and selects a quick route from the search results or dashboard shortcut to begin a task such as editing enrollment, viewing attendance, or updating contact details.
expected_observation: The system opens the selected child or family task directly from the dashboard or search screen with minimal navigation, reducing the need to move through multiple menus.

setup: The daily operations dashboard is visible to a staff member during normal business hours, and routine items such as attendance and immunization status are available.
action: The staff member clicks a quick-access item for attendance or immunization checks from the dashboard.
expected_observation: The system opens the selected routine function immediately from the dashboard and displays the relevant list or check screen without requiring the staff member to navigate through the full menu structure.

setup: The organization has scheduled a phased rollout with staff training, a parallel running period, and a planned cutover date. Both the legacy process and the new system are available during the parallel period.
action: Trained staff perform the same operational task in both the legacy process and the new system during parallel run, then the cutover is initiated on the planned date.
expected_observation: The system supports the training and parallel operation period, allows comparison of results during rollout, and transitions to full cutover only when the planned cutover is approved.

setup: An authorized staff member is out of office and a designated backup has been granted temporary coverage for specific duties only, such as attendance or pickup authorization review.
action: The backup staff member signs in and attempts to perform both a covered duty and an uncovered duty, then the coverage is removed or expires when the primary staff member returns.
expected_observation: The system grants the backup access only to the covered duties, blocks access to unrelated functions, and automatically ends or easily removes the temporary access when coverage ends.

setup: A shared workstation is used by multiple staff members during the day, and each user has their own credentials.
action: One staff member logs in, completes work, signs out or switches user, and another staff member logs in on the same workstation.
expected_observation: The system supports fast authentication and user switching on the shared workstation, shows the correct user context after each switch, and prevents one staff member from continuing under another staff member's session.

setup: The system is accessed from both a shared desktop computer at the front desk and a tablet used in the classroom.
action: A staff member opens the system on each device and performs a common task such as viewing attendance or updating a child record.
expected_observation: The system displays and operates correctly on both the shared desktop and the tablet, with usable screens and controls appropriate to each device type.

setup: A migration package is prepared for go-live containing active family accounts, enrolled children, classroom assignments, immunization status, balances, waiting list entries, contact history, and authorized pickup lists.
action: The migration is executed into the live system at go-live.
expected_observation: The system imports the specified active records and preserves the listed data elements so staff can continue operations with current family, child, billing, and contact information available after go-live.

setup: A staff member is assigned to one site only, and another user has a cross-site administrative role. Records exist for multiple sites.
action: Each user opens child, family, or classroom records from the system.
expected_observation: The site-based staff member can only see and manage records for their own site, while the cross-site user can access records across sites according to their elevated role.

setup: A family has children enrolled at two different sites, with one shared parent contact record and one shared billing account.
action: A staff member views the family account from either site and updates the contact phone number or reviews the billing balance.
expected_observation: The system keeps one unified family account, shows both children across sites under that account, and preserves shared contact and billing information instead of splitting the family into separate site-specific accounts.

setup: Two or more siblings are linked within a family account and are enrolled at different locations. An authorized user has permission to view multi-site reports.
action: The authorized user opens a sibling or family report that spans locations.
expected_observation: The system rolls up the sibling information across locations for the authorized user and displays the combined results in the report.

setup: A user with export or import permission is working with child care records that need to be shared externally or loaded from another system.
action: The user exports a selected dataset to CSV and then imports a prepared CSV file containing family or child records; where supported, the user also requests Excel or PDF output for appropriate reports.
expected_observation: The system produces CSV export files, accepts CSV imports, and provides Excel or PDF output when appropriate for the selected data or report.

setup: An import file contains a mix of valid rows and rows with missing values, mismatched field types, or values outside allowed ranges. Existing records are already present in the system.
action: A user submits the import file for processing.
expected_observation: The system validates each field in each row, rejects only the affected row or record with clear error details, imports the valid rows, and leaves all existing data unchanged.

setup: A staff member is signed into Nenios with a role that includes export/import privileges. The family record contains sensitive child and guardian details, including medical notes, emergency contacts, and protected identifiers.
action: The staff member attempts to export the family record and then imports a data file containing sensitive fields that are not approved for that role.
expected_observation: The system allows export or import only for the fields permitted by the user's security role and policy, omits restricted sensitive fields, and blocks the unauthorized import with a clear permission error and an explanation of which fields are not allowed.

setup: An invoice has already been issued to a family for monthly tuition and is posted in the billing ledger.
action: A billing staff member enters a correction for the invoice amount because a charge needs to be reduced.
expected_observation: The system creates a separate invoice adjustment record that increases or decreases the balance as appropriate, keeps the original charge intact, and shows the adjustment on the invoice history instead of rewriting the original invoice line.

setup: A posted tuition charge has been flagged by a parent as disputed and is awaiting review by billing staff.
action: A billing staff member opens the family account and views the disputed invoice list.
expected_observation: The disputed charge remains visible with a clear dispute status, appears in billing review queues or invoice history, and is not removed or hidden from staff until the dispute is resolved.

setup: A family has an original invoice with an outstanding balance, and billing staff are authorized to issue credits and refunds.
action: The staff member records a credit or refund against the invoice and enters the reason for the correction.
expected_observation: The system saves the credit or refund with a required reason, links it to the original invoice, and shows the transaction in the invoice ledger with the updated balance.

setup: An invoice adjustment, credit, refund, or reversal has been performed by an authorized user in the billing area.
action: An administrator opens the audit history for the affected invoice or family account.
expected_observation: The system displays an audit trail showing who made each change, when it occurred, what type of billing action was taken, and the stated reason or note for the change.

setup: A family account has two enrolled children, both eligible for tuition billing, and staff have configured a sibling discount policy for the site.
action: Billing is generated for the billing cycle in which both children are active under the same family account.
expected_observation: The system applies the configured sibling discount only to eligible tuition charges, shows the discount on the invoice, and does not apply it when the policy is not configured or the children are not both eligible.

setup: An invoice has passed its due date and the configured grace period has elapsed without payment.
action: The billing cycle is recalculated or the overdue account is refreshed by staff.
expected_observation: The system adds the configured late fee to the invoice, displays the fee as a separate charge, and does not apply the fee before the grace period has expired.

setup: A child starts enrollment partway through the billing period, leaves mid-cycle, or has an enrollment change that affects billable days.
action: The billing run is generated for that period.
expected_observation: The system prorates the tuition based on the active enrollment dates or changed enrollment status and shows the prorated amount on the invoice instead of charging the full period amount.

setup: A configurable attendance policy is in place that defines whether absences reduce tuition, and a child has recorded absences during the billing period.
action: The billing calculation is run for the child under the configured absence policy.
expected_observation: The system applies tuition effects only according to the configured policy, such as reducing or not reducing charges based on the defined rules, and does not use a fixed hardcoded absence rule.

setup: A sensitive change request is pending, such as an enrollment exception, capacity override, payment reversal, or temporary access grant, and an authorized reviewer is available.
action: The authorized user reviews the request and chooses to approve, override, or reject it.
expected_observation: The system requires an authorized decision before the exception takes effect, records the reviewer's action, and updates the related child, family, or billing record only according to the approved outcome.

setup: A child is being brought into Nenios with immunization records that are incomplete, overdue, or missing at go-live.
action: The child record is imported or activated for enrollment review.
expected_observation: The child remains enrolled or provisionally active as allowed by policy, is clearly marked as not compliant, and the compliance status is visible to staff instead of blocking the record outright.

setup: A child record is marked as having missing or noncompliant immunization documentation, and staff need to complete follow-up.
action: A staff member opens the immunization follow-up workflow and updates the record after receiving new documentation.
expected_observation: The system provides a clear follow-up path showing outstanding requirements, contact or verification status, and completion history, and the noncompliant status is cleared only after the record is verified or updated.

setup: A user signs into Nenios with a standard staff role that needs access to everyday operations.
action: The user lands on the home page or navigates to the main staff screen.
expected_observation: The system presents a central dashboard or search screen that provides access to common daily tasks such as child lookup, family lookup, billing review, attendance, and notifications.

setup: A rollout plan is in place for a new Nenios installation, with training sessions scheduled for administrators, office staff, classroom staff, and read-only users.
action: The training and access plan is executed for the different staff groups.
expected_observation: The system supports onboarding administrators and office staff first, then classroom staff and other users afterward, with access and training materials aligned to each role's need to view child or family information.

setup: Core child, family, enrollment, and billing data have been loaded into Nenios, and the staff have completed rehearsal of the main workflows.
action: The organization initiates go-live approval.
expected_observation: The system allows go-live to proceed only when core data loading is complete and the main workflows can be completed reliably, and it prevents go-live approval when those readiness conditions are not met.

setup: The center is preparing for full cutover and has current reports, billing records, and attendance logs generated from the new system alongside the expected center output from the legacy process.
action: An authorized operations user compares the new system's report totals, billing summaries, and attendance counts against the expected center output before approving cutover.
expected_observation: The system shows matching figures for reports, billing, and attendance, or clearly flags any discrepancies so staff can correct them before full cutover.

setup: A classroom is already at its defined capacity, and a child is currently assigned to that room.
action: A staff member attempts to move another child into the full classroom without using an override, then repeats the move with an authorized override request.
expected_observation: The first move is blocked because the classroom is full; the override path allows the move only for an authorized user and records the exception.

setup: A staff user attempts to edit a child record in a way that changes custody status, pickup authorization, allergy-related safety handling, immunization compliance, or billing arrangements.
action: The user submits the change for approval.
expected_observation: The system routes the pending change to staff review and does not apply it until a reviewer approves it.

setup: A child has a documented severe allergy and a restricted pickup list on file, and the child is checked out at the end of the day.
action: A staff member opens the release screen for that child.
expected_observation: The allergy alert and restricted pickup information are shown immediately and prominently before the child can be released.

setup: The center is in a peak operational period with end-of-day reporting, invoice review, routine record updates, and billing edits pending.
action: Staff submit several non-urgent tasks during the busy period.
expected_observation: The system places non-urgent work into a queue or delayed processing state, while continuing to prioritize urgent operational tasks without interruption.

setup: A staff member is viewing a child record that includes compliance items such as immunization, forms, and other tracked requirements.
action: The staff member scans the summary list without opening the detailed record.
expected_observation: Each item is clearly marked as current, due soon, overdue, exempt, or missing, allowing the staff member to know the next follow-up action at a glance.

setup: A user is signed in with a role that is either administrative, authorized staff, or a general staff role.
action: The user attempts to access enrollment, capacity, billing, or record management functions.
expected_observation: Only administrators and authorized staff can complete these actions; unauthorized users are denied access or shown read-only restrictions.

setup: A teaching staff member or support staff member is signed in and opens a child or family profile.
action: The user tries to view sensitive billing information or open full administrative settings.
expected_observation: The system hides or blocks access to sensitive billing data and full administrative controls for teaching and support staff.

setup: A non-system-administrator user is signed in and can access ordinary operational screens.
action: The user attempts to change security settings, user permissions, or other system-wide configuration values.
expected_observation: The system prevents the change and allows only a system administrator to modify security and global configuration settings.

setup: A report export is being generated that may contain custody, contact, payment, health, or special needs information, and the user is signed in with a role that is not administrator, senior administrator, or authorized supervisor.
action: The user requests to view the export details.
expected_observation: Unmasked sensitive export details are not shown to the user unless they have one of the permitted elevated roles.

setup: A routine operational export is being prepared for a staff user who does not have a business need for sensitive data.
action: The user generates the export.
expected_observation: Sensitive fields are excluded or masked by default, and the export contains only the minimum information needed for routine operations.

setup: A staff member generates an export containing child and family information.
action: The export is created without an explicit exception for sensitive disclosure.
expected_observation: The export masks or omits full custody details, emergency contacts, full payment information, health or immunization notes, special needs notes, custody restrictions, and similar staff-inappropriate fields.

setup: A classroom has already reached its maximum approved capacity.
action: A staff user attempts to enroll an additional child into that classroom.
expected_observation: The enrollment is blocked by default and the system shows that the classroom cannot accept additional children unless capacity is changed through an approved path.

setup: A billing account already has a sibling discount applied and another discount type is available for the same charge period.
action: A staff member attempts to apply the additional discount to the same invoice.
expected_observation: The system prevents the sibling discount from stacking with the other discount unless the policy explicitly permits the combination.

setup: A user with a non-payment role is signed in and opens a billing or payment screen.
action: The user attempts to enter a new payment or modify an existing payment record.
expected_observation: The system blocks the action unless the user has the required permission to create or change payments.

setup: A family account has been marked for an exceptional billing situation, and an administrator has opened a temporary access request form in the child care management system.
action: The administrator approves temporary access by entering a specific billing reason and selecting an expiration date for the access window.
expected_observation: The system grants access only for the selected time period, records the stated reason in the account history, and displays the temporary access as time-limited rather than permanent.

setup: A staff member is reviewing incoming tuition payments, and one payment matches a risk condition such as a very large amount, a payment immediately after a dispute, a failed-payment account, an inactive payer, a heavily overdue balance, or a suspicious pattern.
action: The staff member submits the payment for processing.
expected_observation: The system holds the payment for review instead of posting it immediately and shows that the hold was triggered by the identified risk condition.

setup: A family with an active recurring tuition schedule has a normal monthly payment due, and no account problems or payment irregularities are present.
action: The scheduled tuition payment is processed on its due date.
expected_observation: The payment posts immediately without manual review, and the account ledger shows the recurring tuition payment as completed successfully.

setup: The attendance dashboard is open during a peak arrival or pickup period with multiple staff members recording attendance at the same time.
action: Staff rapidly check in or check out several children in succession while the system is under heavy use.
expected_observation: Attendance entries are saved promptly, the interface remains usable, and no attendance action times out or becomes unresponsive during the peak period.

setup: An administrator is importing migration data that contains missing, inconsistent, mismatched, or conflicting values for some source records that already exist in the system.
action: The administrator runs the import or migration process without manually resolving the conflicting rows first.
expected_observation: The system does not silently replace existing source records, and it reports the affected records with clear conflict or validation notices instead of overwriting them.

setup: A staff user is viewing a child, enrollment, or attendance data set that is available for file transfer.
action: The staff user exports the selected records to a CSV file and then imports a CSV file containing matching record fields.
expected_observation: The system produces a valid CSV file for export and successfully reads CSV input, preserving field structure and record values in the imported data.

setup: A staff user has a spreadsheet file containing child care records in a supported Excel workbook format.
action: The staff user imports the Excel file or exports selected records to an Excel workbook.
expected_observation: The system accepts the Excel workbook for import or creates an Excel-formatted export when the feature is enabled, with the data available in spreadsheet form afterward.

setup: A user has generated a report or record set that is intended for viewing only, such as a billing summary or attendance report.
action: The user requests a PDF export of the report.
expected_observation: The system creates a PDF document that opens as read-only content and preserves the report layout for viewing or printing without editable fields.

setup: An import file is prepared with required person and child data fields including names, dates, phone numbers, emails, and immunization dates, and at least one row contains an invalid or missing value in one of these fields.
action: The staff user uploads the file for import validation.
expected_observation: The system flags the invalid rows with field-specific validation messages for the missing or malformed name, date, phone number, email, or immunization date values and does not accept those invalid entries as valid records.

setup: An import file contains multiple rows, and one row includes a missing, mismatched, or out-of-range value while other rows are valid.
action: The staff user starts the import process.
expected_observation: The system rejects only the affected row or record, keeps the existing data unchanged for that record, and imports the other valid rows successfully.

setup: Staff are working in the child care management system to update child profiles, attendance, billing, and communications during normal daily operations.
action: They complete routine tasks such as searching records, entering attendance, and saving updates across several modules.
expected_observation: The system responds quickly, maintains consistent results across repeated actions, and helps staff complete tasks accurately without conflicting outputs or delayed updates.

setup: A child record already exists with contact, enrollment, and billing information in the system.
action: A staff member edits the record and attempts to enter the same household, contact, or tuition information again in a separate form or screen.
expected_observation: The system reuses existing information where possible, avoids creating duplicate entries, and reduces the need for the staff member to retype the same data in multiple places.

setup: A staff member is using the main dashboard on a standard office display and needs to move between attendance, billing, and family records.
action: The staff member navigates through the menus and reads on-screen labels, buttons, and record details.
expected_observation: The screens are easy to read, labels are clear, navigation is straightforward, and the staff member can find common functions without confusion.

setup: A staff member is opening a page with action buttons, checkboxes, or other form controls on a typical desktop browser.
action: The staff member attempts to use the available controls to complete a common task such as saving a record or marking attendance.
expected_observation: The controls are large enough to select comfortably and are not tiny or cramped, allowing the task to be completed without repeated misclicks.

setup: The center is experiencing a busy arrival, pickup, or meal-time period with many staff members entering attendance and meal records at the same time.
action: Multiple users submit records concurrently for several children.
expected_observation: The system remains responsive, continues accepting input without noticeable slowdown or timeouts, and successfully saves the concurrent entries.

setup: The center director is using Nenios on a staff tablet while a small issue has been reported in a classroom check-in workflow, and the system has an available support path for help or escalation.
action: The director opens the help or support option from the affected screen and submits a support request describing the issue.
expected_observation: The system presents a simple, easy-to-follow support experience, records the issue without data loss, and confirms that help has been requested through an acknowledgment or ticket reference.

setup: Nenios is already configured with one site and several classrooms, and an administrator is preparing to expand the center's structure for future growth.
action: The administrator adds a new classroom and a new site using the existing configuration screens.
expected_observation: The system accepts the new classroom and site without requiring a rebuild or replacement of existing records, and the newly added locations appear alongside the current structure with the existing data preserved.

setup: The center has reached capacity in its current building, and management needs to model an additional classroom and a second site for an upcoming expansion.
action: The administrator creates additional classroom records and registers a new site, then assigns children and staff to the new location.
expected_observation: The system accommodates the added classrooms and site cleanly, updates the organizational structure, and allows the new spaces to be used for scheduling and enrollment without disrupting the original site.

setup: Front-desk staff use a shared desktop computer at check-in, and classroom teachers use tablets for attendance and child records.
action: A staff member signs in, opens attendance, and completes a routine check-in on both the desktop and the tablet.
expected_observation: The screens render correctly and remain usable on both device types, key actions are accessible without layout breakage, and common tasks such as check-in and record viewing can be completed comfortably on shared desktops and tablets.

setup: A shared workstation at the front desk is used by multiple employees throughout the day, and staff need a fast way to access the system without repeatedly typing full credentials.
action: An authorized staff member selects the quick login option on the shared workstation and completes a rapid sign-in process.
expected_observation: The system signs the staff member in quickly with the shared-workstation login method, grants access to the appropriate staff workspace, and makes the process suitable for repeated use on a common desk terminal.

setup: Several noncritical tasks are already queued in the system, such as report generation or background updates, while a child needs to be marked present at the front desk.
action: A staff member performs the attendance action to check a child in while the background tasks remain pending.
expected_observation: The attendance action completes promptly and reliably without being blocked by the queued work, and the child's attendance status updates immediately for staff use.

setup: A classroom roster is open for a teacher, and some children have complete immunization records while others have missing or due items; the room is near its enrollment limit.
action: The teacher views the roster or dashboard summary for immunization and classroom capacity status.
expected_observation: The system shows clear at-a-glance indicators for each child's immunization status and the classroom's current capacity, allowing the teacher or manager to identify compliance issues and occupancy status without opening each record individually.

setup: The center calendar includes a major holiday, a school break, and a staff training day, and staff are preparing the schedule for the affected period.
action: A scheduler opens the calendar and reviews the days marked as holiday, break, and training day.
expected_observation: The system treats those days as scheduling exceptions, displays them distinctly on the calendar, and applies the exception status automatically so staff do not need to work around them manually.

setup: A school break or staff training day has been defined on the center calendar, and management wants a reduced operating plan for that period.
action: The scheduler assigns a reduced classroom schedule or special staffing plan for the break or training day.
expected_observation: The system allows the special schedule to be created for the exception period and displays the reduced or alternate plan on the affected dates without treating it as a normal operating day.

setup: A classroom has already reached its normal capacity, and a manager has a documented exceptional reason to temporarily admit one additional child.
action: The manager attempts to override the classroom capacity limit for that child enrollment.
expected_observation: The system allows the override only through manager or administrator authority, records the exception in the audit trail with the user and reason, and makes the override visible in the classroom capacity status.

setup: A child is ready to be released, but the system detects missing allergy information, conflicting pickup authorization, or another incomplete safety detail in the child's record.
action: A staff member attempts to release the child to a pickup person despite the incomplete or conflicting safety data.
expected_observation: The system holds the release for review, prevents the child from being released normally, and alerts staff that the safety information must be resolved before the release can proceed.

setup: The center has an active policy that permits temporary immunization exceptions under defined conditions, and a child's immunization record is currently noncompliant.
action: An administrator applies a temporary immunization exception for the child under the center's policy.
expected_observation: The system allows the exception only because the policy exists, records the temporary exception according to policy, and makes the child's nonstandard immunization status visible in the compliance display.

setup: A payment reversal is being requested, and the center has configured approval rules that require extra review for unusual or high-value reversals.
action: A staff member submits a small reversal and then attempts a large or unusual reversal.
expected_observation: The small reversal follows the configured approval path, while the large or unusual reversal is routed to second review or manager approval and cannot be completed immediately without that additional authorization.

setup: The system contains a site with rooms that may be categorized either as separate program types or as classroom categories, and the product team has not finalized which model applies.
action: An administrator attempts to classify a room using the available setup screens and then views how the room is represented in reports and schedules.
expected_observation: The system exposes a clear room classification model in the user interface consistent with the chosen design, and the room appears in setup, scheduling, and reporting according to that model without ambiguity between program type and classroom category.

setup: Multiple sites and programs exist, and the exact operating times for each site or program are still awaiting verification from the center.
action: A scheduler opens the site or program setup and attempts to define operating hours for each location.
expected_observation: The system supports a clearly presented operating-hours configuration boundary for sites or programs, and the resulting schedule display reflects whatever verified hours have been entered without assuming unconfirmed times.

setup: The initial release of Nenios Child Care Management is already in use by staff and parents, and the product backlog contains proposed future enhancements including richer parent communication, online forms, more detailed reporting, online payment processing, and automated reminders.
action: A product stakeholder reviews the unresolved enhancement list and attempts to confirm which feature will be scheduled first for the next implementation phase.
expected_observation: The system or project records indicate that no implementation priority has been finalized yet, and the unresolved status remains visible for the enhancement set without assigning a first-release priority to any one item.
